To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we devise and analyze an algorithm for radar space-time code design that is able to achieve the desired performance in the presence of a non-white Gaussian disturbance.

we propose a new code design algorithm, which maximizes the detection performance in STAP, under a control on temporal and spatial estimation accuracy and on the degree (in terms of similarity) with a pre-fixed code.

(i) the new code design algorithm is effective for the radar STAP task; (ii) the new algorithm outperforms the existing ones in terms of detection performance; (iii) the new algorithm is robust to the uncertainty of the disturbance covariance matrix; (iv) the new algorithm provides a good trade-off among the different performance requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: 1) code design for radar space-time processing; 2) semidefinite relaxation of nonconvex quadratic problems; 3) rank-one decomposition of semidefinite matrices; 4) performance assessment on simulated and real data; 5) code optimization for radar STAP.
the design of radar STAP codes by means of convex optimization theory.

the following topics: (i) the development of a new algorithm for radar code optimization; (ii) the assessment of the algorithm on simulated data and real data; (iii) the comparison of the new algorithm with the existing ones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our algorithm is capable of designing radar codes for STAP with a good trade-off among the different performance indexes.
our new approach is a promising tool to design radar STAP codes, which can be successfully used in a variety of applications.
, in the presence of a colored Gaussian noise, the proposed code design method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed code optimization algorithm can be applied to the problem of radar STAP code design, and can be used to devise new radar waveforms with enhanced detection performance.

we have proposed a code design algorithm that can be used to design codes for radar STAP in the presence of correlated Gaussian disturbance, and which is able to guarantee the achievement of a pre-specified level of Doppler estimation accuracy.

, by resorting to the proposed code design approach, we can obtain a radar code that, on the one hand, maximizes the detection performance, and, on the other, guarantees a good degree of similarity with the pre-fixed radar code.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the new code design method allows for a significant improvement in the detection performance with respect to the state-of-the-art methods, while preserving the same degree of similarity with the pre-fixed code.
the proposed algorithm is able to design codes that outperform existing ones in terms of detection capability while maintaining similar degrees of similarity with a given radar code.
the proposed approach can be applied to the design of STAP codes with a performance comparable with the one of the state-of-the-art algorithms, but with a reduced computational complexity.
